issues.acceptance: An external focusboard:// activation captured by the registered native replay returns to the app (warm) or boots into the verified state (cold) with the token consumed exactly once, and a reused or expired token lands in the recoverable expired-link state; the paste fallback stays functional.
issues.actual: src-tauri/src/lib.rs implements register_scheme() (writes focusboard.desktop with MimeType x-scheme-handler/focusboard, runs xdg-mime), warm forwarding over focusboard-deeplink.sock, cold-arg PendingDeepLink, and App.tsx auto-verifies take_deep_link tokens without rendering them; capabilities/main.json grants only core:event:default and the CSP is unchanged. However replay.json and capture_evidence.json contain no external link-activation scenario (golden_path unavailable; renderer text is auth-shell only), so the developer-reported warm/cold Xvfb validation is not observable through the registered runtime contract. Paste fallback remains functional at store level; per the plan stop condition the route is reported not-runtime-proven rather than failed.

implied_completion: The scheduler implies persisted, restart-safe state: reminders scheduled before a full app restart still fire after it.
Replacing the placeholders implies removing the deferred nav flags and soon badges in src/App.tsx.
Mail-sink delivery implies no real SMTP provider or network dependency is introduced this loop.
Golden-path completability implies the previously undrivable prefix (register through restart) also becomes drivable, since the replay runs one continuous path.
An idempotent scheduler implies a deduplication key that survives retries without duplicate emails for one task and schedule.
The deferred issues (deeplink recapture, rustfmt, white-box lane, signed-in captures) are not prerequisites for closing this increment and receive no current-loop disposition.
mandatory_objectives: PRD section 3 steps 6-8 and 10 become performable: reminder time and timezone set on a task, calendar placement confirmed, focus session completed, reminder email received.
Reminder and FocusSession follow PRD sections 5 and 7 semantics: persisted entities, idempotent dispatch, delivery states, and cancel-on-complete-or-delete.
Calendar, Focus, and Settings replace all deferred placeholders and satisfy PRD section 8 surface and state requirements for every reachable state.
The full section 3 path is drivable end to end through the live UI and typed IPC so the host replay can recapture golden_path receipts that no longer report state unavailable.
Frozen baselines hold: least-privilege capabilities, unchanged CSP, preserved auth and token hygiene, clean builds, and no visual regression of the validated auth shell.
task_specification.objective: Make the release-critical PRD section 3 first-run path completable end to end: implement the Reminder entity with timezone-aware idempotent scheduling and mail-sink delivery, the FocusSession model with a full session lifecycle, and real Calendar, Focus, and Settings surfaces replacing the deferred placeholders, so the registered native replay can drive the whole path through live UI/IPC and recapture golden_path receipts that no longer report state unavailable.

diagnosis.root_cause: The release-critical PRD section 3 path cannot be performed because the candidate deferred its core surfaces: src/App.tsx renders DeferredSurface placeholders for calendar, focus, and settings (lines 427-429, nav entries flagged deferred), and src-tauri implements no Reminder entity, no scheduler, and no FocusSession model. Prior loop budget went to deep-link instrumentation while these stayed deferred, so the registered replay still has no completable path to drive and every bound receipt reports golden_path.state=unavailable. The defect is missing product capability, not instrumentation.

stop_conditions: Stop and escalate if a compliant scheduler or reminder delivery requires widening src-tauri/capabilities/main.json beyond the current least-privilege grant or touching the CSP string.
Stop and escalate if reminder email would require a real SMTP provider or external network service instead of the existing local mail sink.
Stop and report blocked if completing a section 3 step as written would break the preserved auth, token-hygiene, or recovery posture; compose with the validated auth shell rather than replacing it.
Stop and report blocked if any section 3 step is unimplementable without changing PRD meaning; never silently narrow the release-critical path.
Stop and report blocked if the increment would require editing run-owned evidence or replay tooling rather than candidate files; that is a role boundary, not a fix.

strategy.rationale: Loop 3 spent its budget on deep-link instrumentation while the golden-path surfaces stayed placeholders, so the replay had nothing drivable. This loop flips to direct implementation of the missing domain model (Reminder, scheduler, FocusSession) and the three deferred surfaces, which is exactly what the pinned blocker's retest recipe names. It is a materially different root-cause strategy than prior deferral-then-instrumentation, and recapture stays host-owned validation.

code: Fresh clean builds exit 0 on the candidate: npm ci and npm run build (tsc --noEmit plus vite build), and cargo build or cargo check under src-tauri.
White-box cargo tests cover scheduler idempotency, timezone conversion, cancel-on-complete, and token-free reminder email content alongside the existing five passing tests.
runtime: Host-owned focusboard-native-webdriver replay drives the full PRD section 3 path through the live UI and IPC — register, mail-sink verify, sign in, create project, create task with reminder and timezone, calendar check, focus session, complete, reminder email, logout and sign back in — and exports candidate-bound runtime_state and screenshot receipts.
Inside the replay, a full app restart preserves the task, reminder, and settings, and the receipts no longer report golden_path.state=unavailable.
visual: Fresh captures show the real Calendar, Focus, and Settings surfaces plus Today's completion summary, matching the PRD section 9 calm editorial direction with no auth-shell regression.
The captured reminder email and delivery states show task title and local time with no tokens or private content exposed.

done_when: A task with a reminder time and timezone can be created from the signed-in UI, appears in Inbox, Today, Projects, and the correct Calendar date, and persists across a full app restart.
Focus mode starts, pauses, resumes, and completes a session bound to one task; completion is recorded exactly once and the Today summary updates.
A due reminder delivers exactly one mail-sink email containing the task title and due context, and completing the task cancels its pending reminder with a skipped delivery state.
Calendar, Focus, and Settings are real surfaces reachable from primary navigation with no DeferredSurface placeholder or soon badge remaining.
Settings shows the user profile, timezone, notification preference, and reminder delivery states with a retry action for failed delivery.
Least-privilege capabilities and the CSP string are unchanged, and clean npm and cargo builds exit 0.

evidence_resolution.rationale: find.first-run-gui-drive-missing is evidence-stalled because the path the registered instruments must drive does not exist in the candidate: the replay reports golden_path.state=unavailable since steps 6-8 and 10 cannot be performed. This task builds the missing surfaces and exposes them through stable, drivable live UI and typed IPC so the registered focusboard-native-webdriver replay and focusboard-verify exporter can produce candidate-bound receipts; the recapture itself remains host-owned validation, never a developer task.

tasks.instructions: Implement the missing golden-path capability so PRD section 3 is completable end to end. Backend (src-tauri): add the Reminder entity (task id, user id, scheduled instant, timezone, channel, status, provider message id, sent timestamp, retry count, deduplication key) and the FocusSession entity per PRD section 5, persisted through the existing SQLite store with migrations; run an idempotent, restart-safe scheduler that dispatches due reminders through the existing mail-sink channel with PRD section 7 delivery states, cancels pending reminders when a task is completed or deleted, and never duplicates sends for one task and schedule. Frontend (src): replace the three DeferredSurface placeholders in src/App.tsx (calendar, focus, settings) with real surfaces: Calendar with month and agenda views in the user's timezone; Focus with start, pause, resume, finish, and cancel, task title visible, and session history; Settings with profile, timezone, notification preferences, and reminder delivery states with a retry action. Let task create and edit set a reminder time and timezone; Today shows overdue, due-today, scheduled focus work, and a completion summary. Keep every step drivable through the live UI and typed IPC with stable, meaningful element identities so the registered native replay can drive the full path; never add QA banners, test ledgers, or probe counters to the product UI. Preserve frozen baselines: least-privilege capabilities and CSP unchanged, auth and token hygiene untouched, clean npm and cargo builds exit 0. Module split within src-tauri/src and src/views is the developer's choice; do not modify run-owned evidence or touch deferred issues.

risk_note.summary: Highest insufficiency risk is runtime recapture: even with all surfaces implemented, the host replay may fail to drive the full path (selector drift, scheduler not firing inside the replay window), returning insufficient evidence for prd_golden_path again.
risk_note.validation: Keep every step drivable through live UI/IPC with stable meaningful element identities, self-drive the whole section 3 path in developer validation before handoff, and report any replay-side blocker explicitly instead of claiming completion.
risk_note.why_now: find.golden-path-surfaces-missing is the host-pinned blocker and the scheduler's selected product finding, and every bound receipt currently reports golden_path.state=unavailable.
